post_title: What national wholesale price for graded, loose, white Large shell eggs will the USDA AMS Egg Markets Overview dated November 13, 2026 report? (cents per dozen)

question.title: What national wholesale price for graded, loose, white Large shell eggs will the USDA AMS Egg Markets Overview dated November 13, 2026 report? (cents per dozen)
question.description:
The USDA Agricultural Marketing Service's "Egg Markets Overview" (report slug AMS_3725, issued by Livestock, Poultry and Grain Market News in Des Moines, IA) is a weekly PDF published on Fridays, usually in the afternoon US Central time. Each edition leads with a short narrative on the national shell egg market, and since 2026 the key national benchmark has been the "wholesale prices for national trading of truck lot quantities of graded, loose, white Large shell eggs" — the negotiated, f.o.b.-dock price for trucklot loads of loose (uncartoned) graded Large white eggs, as distinct from the New York formula cartoned price, Midwest warehouse-delivered prices, or California benchmarks.

Status quo (most recent editions):
- October 30, 2026: $0.35/dozen, up $0.07 (New York formula cartoned Large steady at $0.72; Midwest warehouse-delivered Large steady at $0.54; Midwest producer price $0.36; California benchmark up $0.09 to $1.10; average conventional-caged retail ad price up $0.10 to $1.42; shell egg inventory up 7%, national Large inventory up 11%, Midwest Large inventory up 19%; breaking stock down $0.0250 to $0.0800/dozen).
- October 23, 2026: $0.28/dozen, down $0.01 (New York formula $0.72, down $0.04).
- October 16, 2026: $0.29/dozen, down $0.14.
- October 9, 2026: $0.43/dozen, down $0.03.
- September 25, 2026: $0.39/dozen, up $0.04. September 18: $0.35, steady. September 4: $0.35, down $0.04.
- Mid-June 2026: $0.24/dozen, the low for the year. February 27, 2026: $0.37, down $0.15. Early March 2026: $0.74, up $0.37. Late March 2026: $1.17, down $0.34 (implying roughly $1.51 the prior week), the 2026 high.

So the line is volatile: weekly moves of 1–7 cents are routine, moves of 14–37 cents have occurred several times in 2026, and the 2026 range spans roughly $0.24 to about $1.51 per dozen. The most recent reading, $0.35, is near the bottom of that range.

Supply and demand context as of late October 2026:
- Table egg layer flock and production are large. USDA ERS reports an average layer flock of 317.3 million birds in August 2026 and a September 1 table-egg layer inventory of 318.7 million hens, up 5.4% year over year; August table egg production was 676.8 million dozen, up 6.0% year over year. This ample supply helps explain the collapse in negotiated loose-egg prices from spring levels.
- Highly pathogenic avian influenza is an active upside risk. The Scramble's APHIS-based layer-flock tracker counts 18.3 million layer birds affected in 2026 across 15 confirmed layer detections in seven states through October 28, 2026. A 934,600-hen commercial table-egg layer flock in Clinton County, Illinois was confirmed infected on October 19, 2026 (the largest active US outbreak at the time), and a 1.3 million-bird layer detection in California was confirmed on October 28, 2026. Coverage in the week of October 26 noted that the first full week of USDA data after the Illinois detection showed no price jump yet, though depopulations remove supply with a lag of weeks to months.
- Demand seasonality favors higher prices into mid-November: retail baking demand ahead of Thanksgiving (November 26, 2026) and holiday feature activity typically lift cartoned and loose egg prices in the first three weeks of November, and the October 30 report already showed retail ad prices rising.
- Release timing: the monthly NASS "Chickens and Eggs" report is next due around November 20, 2026 and the ERS Livestock, Dairy, and Poultry Outlook around November 17, 2026 — both after the resolution date. The November 13, 2026 Egg Markets Overview is therefore the only in-window authoritative read on this market, and the October 30 and November 6 editions (published before forecasting opens) give forecasters the latest trend.

Useful live sources for forecasters: the AMS report archive (https://mymarketnews.ams.usda.gov/viewReport/3725), APHIS HPAI confirmed detections (https://www.aphis.usda.gov/h5n1-hpai), and The Scramble's layer-flock tracker (https://the-scramble.com/hpai/layer-flocks).

question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves to the single price stated in the USDA AMS "Egg Markets Overview" report dated November 13, 2026, in the sentence reporting the "wholesale prices for national trading of truck lot quantities of graded, loose, white Large shell eggs" (the sentence typically reads like "Wholesale prices for national trading of truck lot quantities of graded, loose, white Large shell eggs were $0.01 lower at $0.28 per dozen with a steady undertone"). The edition is available from the AMS report archive at https://mymarketnews.ams.usda.gov/viewReport/3725 (select the 2026 releases and open the November 13, 2026 PDF) and, on its publication day, at https://www.ams.usda.gov/mnreports/ams_3725.pdf. The value is expressed in cents per dozen: a report stating "$0.35 per dozen" resolves as 35, and a report stating "35 cents per dozen" also resolves as 35. Only that one price counts; other prices in the same report (New York formula cartoned, Midwest warehouse-delivered, Midwest producer, California benchmarks, breaking stock, egg products) are disregarded.
question.fine_print: If the edition dated November 13, 2026 is not published, or is published without this line, this question resolves to the value for the same line in the next edition of the Egg Markets Overview that reports it. If the report stops publishing this line entirely and no later edition reports it, the question is annulled.
